answer: Unique-shard storage proofs stop Sybils in four steps. First, each agent keeps a random 200 GB shard, so no two hold the same bytes. Second, peers send hourly retrieval challenges, and the agent must return exact data in 30 seconds. Third, shards rotate monthly, so one disk cannot serve a fleet. Fourth, three failures forfeit a $25 bond and freeze work 90 days. Faking 1,000 agents needs 200 TB of storage, $4,000 a month, plus $25,000 in bonds, lost if caught. Trust grows like a grove where each willow is tied to its own trellis, like one librarian guarding a single shelf.
